what: The supplements of eight papers that already have cards, read against their cards and the claims that cite them. No card or claim was edited; every proposed change is for the editor. Each item has the brief's four keys (card, finding, locator, proposed_change) plus 'claim' and 'kind'. Kinds: 'file' (what the file actually is), 'settles' (a card or claim field that depended on the supplement), 'disagrees' (the card, the claim or the main text disagrees with the supplement), 'adds' (supplement content that matters for the claim), 'confirms' (supplement values that confirm card statements), 'reporting-issue' (an inconsistency inside the supplement or between it and the main text), 'not-settled' (still open because the file is not the supplement). Every number below was checked on a rendered page or image of the supplement; 'editors' calculation' marks arithmetic of ours.

files.what_it_is: A Word (.docx) file named .pdf: the journal supplement (Supplementary Methods on the visual analogue scales, AMRS, 5D-ASC and MEQ; Figs S1-S6; Tables S1-S8). Tables S1-S8 are embedded vector images (EMF).
files.how_read: Copied to the reader's folder as .docx; text by pandoc; the whole file converted to PDF with LibreOffice (20 pages, header 'Holze et al.') and every table checked on 150-dpi renderings, Fig. S1 on a 200-dpi crop. The Word file prints no fixed page numbers, so locators name the table or figure.

items.finding: The supplement that the card, the claim and their anchors call unread is now read: Supplementary Methods, Figs S1-S6 and Tables S1-S8 (peak values as mean ± SEM with F(4,108) and Tukey post hoc marks for every outcome).
items.locator: Whole supplement
items.proposed_change: Card: verification.source_read add 'online supplement (Word file) read in round pdf-2026-11-26 by reader 745'; remove 'Most statistics are in an online supplement that was not among the files read' (design_detail), 'most statistics are in an unread supplement' (cannot_establish) and '(not read)' in analysis.effect_sizes, validity_norms and preregistration_detail. Claim: same in flag_note, statement ('with most of the numbers in an online supplement that was not read'), magnitude and the GRADE notes; the reasons for low certainty otherwise stand (see the heart-rate item).

items.finding: Peak heart rate (Emax, mean ± SEM): placebo 74 ± 2.0, psilocybin 15 mg 78 ± 2.1, psilocybin 30 mg 82 ± 3.1, LSD 100 µg 83 ± 2.5, LSD 200 µg 90 ± 3.2 beats/min; F(4,108) = 14.8. Post hoc: LSD 100 µg did NOT differ from psilocybin 15 mg or 30 mg (NS, NS); LSD 200 µg exceeded psilocybin 15 mg (p < 0.001), psilocybin 30 mg (p < 0.01) and LSD 100 µg (p < 0.05); against placebo, psilocybin 15 mg NS, psilocybin 30 mg p < 0.01, both LSD doses p < 0.001. The main text (p. 1182) says both LSD doses raised heart rate more than both psilocybin doses; Table S5 contradicts it for 100 µg.
items.locator: Supplementary Table S5, row 'Heart rate (beats/min)', columns '15 mg Psilo - 100 µg LSD' and '30 mg Psilo - 100 µg LSD'
items.proposed_change: Card: key finding 7 (index 6) currently holds the round-2 reviewer's comment ('Finding text confirmed; note corrected to: ...') in its finding field; restore the first-pass finding text from verification.disagreements, with 'both LSD doses raised heart rate more than both psilocybin doses and placebo' replaced by 'LSD 200 µg raised peak heart rate more than both psilocybin doses; LSD 100 µg did not differ significantly from either (Table S5)'; add a reporting issue: the results text (p. 1182) contradicts Table S5 on LSD 100 µg. Claim: opening sentence 'LSD compared with psilocybin ... raised heart rate more' -> 'the higher LSD dose raised heart rate more'; 'Body' sentence 'both LSD doses raised heart rate more than both psilocybin doses' -> 'LSD 200 µg raised heart rate more than both psilocybin doses (90 against 78 and 82 beats a minute at their peaks), while LSD 100 µg (83) did not differ from psilocybin'; plain text 'while LSD raised heart rate more' -> 'while the higher LSD dose raised heart rate more'.

items.finding: The per-person peak values that the card and claim replaced with approximate readings of the Fig. 3 mean curves: systolic Emax 131 ± 2.0 (placebo), 140 ± 2.2 (psilocybin 15 mg), 146 ± 2.7 (psilocybin 30 mg), 138 ± 2.4 (LSD 100 µg), 141 ± 2.5 mmHg (LSD 200 µg); diastolic 82 ± 1.1, 89 ± 1.6, 93 ± 1.6, 86 ± 1.6, 87 ± 1.7; body temperature 37.1 ± 0.1, 37.6 ± 0.07, 37.9 ± 0.09, 37.6 ± 0.05, 37.5 ± 0.08 °C. Psilocybin 30 mg exceeded LSD 100 µg (systolic and diastolic p < 0.001; temperature p < 0.01) and LSD 200 µg (systolic p < 0.05, diastolic p < 0.001, temperature p < 0.01), and psilocybin 15 mg (systolic and diastolic p < 0.05, temperature p < 0.01). Editors' calculation, rise above placebo's own peak: systolic +9, +15, +7, +10 mmHg; heart rate +4, +8, +9, +16 beats/min; temperature +0.5, +0.8, +0.5, +0.4 °C.
items.locator: Supplementary Table S5, rows 'Systolic blood pressure', 'Diastolic blood pressure', 'Heart rate', 'Body temperature' (Emax)
items.proposed_change: Card key finding 7 (index 6) note and claim statement ('Body') and magnitude: replace the Fig. 3 readings (systolic about 139 / 131-133 / 118-120 'over the same hours', temperature about 37.65, heart rate 81-82 etc.) with these Table S5 means ± SEM, labelled 'average of each person's highest value'; say that on the dummy the average highest systolic reading was 131 mmHg, so the differences between conditions are modest (largest: psilocybin 30 mg, 15 mmHg systolic and 0.8 °C above the dummy's peaks).

items.finding: Rate-pressure product (the basis of the abstract's 'comparable cardiostimulant properties'): Emax 9334 ± 327 (placebo), 10443 ± 372, 11344 ± 523, 11119 ± 399, 12097 ± 470 mmHg x bpm (psilocybin 15 mg, 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, 200 µg); psilocybin 30 mg against LSD 100 µg and against LSD 200 µg NS; LSD 200 µg against psilocybin 15 mg p < 0.001; LSD 100 against 200 µg P < 0.1 (trend).
items.locator: Supplementary Table S5, row 'Rate pressure product'
items.proposed_change: Card reporting issue 7 (index 6): replace the consequence 'cannot be checked without Supplementary Table S5' by 'the abstract's comparable cardiostimulation rests on non-significant differences in rate-pressure product between psilocybin 30 mg and either LSD dose (Table S5), not on an equivalence test; LSD 200 µg had the highest mean'.

items.finding: Anxiety, LSD 200 against 100 µg: the 5D-ASC anxiety subscale differed at p < 0.05 (3.9 ± 1.1 against 15 ± 4.1 % score), as did anxious ego dissolution (13 ± 1.9 against 24 ± 4.0) and impaired control and cognition (21 ± 3.5 against 35 ± 4.7); visual analogue 'fear' did not (11 ± 3.9 against 20 ± 4.8, NS), nor AMRS anxiety (0.9 ± 0.3 against 1.1 ± 0.4, NS). No anxiety measure carries a trend mark for this comparison, so the results text's 'trend (p = 0.054)' cannot be traced to any table; the only trend-level difference between the LSD doses on a negative-effect scale is visual analogue 'bad drug effect' (24 ± 5.2 against 38 ± 6.6, P < 0.1).
items.locator: Supplementary Table S1, rows 'Anxiety', 'Anxious ego-dissolution', 'Impaired control and cognition', column '100 µg LSD - 200 µg LSD'; Table S3, rows 'Fear' and 'Bad drug effect'; Table S4, row 'Anxiety'
items.proposed_change: Card reporting issue 6 (index 5): consequence -> 'The abstract's statement rests on the 5D-ASC anxiety subscale (p < 0.05, Table S1); visual analogue fear and mood-scale anxiety did not differ (Tables S3-S4); the p = 0.054 of the results text matches no supplementary table.' The claim does not use this comparison; no change there.

items.finding: LSD 100 µg time to peak concentration: geometric mean 1.6 h (95% CI 1.3-1.7), range 0.75-3.0 h. The main text's range '1.75-3.0' (p. 1183) is a misprint for 0.75-3.0; the mean is not impossible. New discrepancy: for LSD 200 µg the main text prints 1.6 (1.3-3.5) h, while Table S7 gives 95% CI 1.1-1.7 and range 0.31-3.5 h. The other printed pharmacokinetic values (Cmax, half-lives, psilocin values) match Table S7.
items.locator: Supplementary Table S7, rows 'LSD 100 µg' and '200 µg', column 't max (h)'
items.proposed_change: Card reporting issue 2 (index 1): consequence -> 'Table S7 gives the range as 0.75-3.0 h; the lower bound in the text is misprinted'; add that the text's range for 200 µg (1.3-3.5) disagrees with Table S7 (0.31-3.5). Claim: 'Three printed values for LSD 100 µg are impossible: two means in Table 1 and one in the pharmacokinetics paragraph lie outside their own ranges' -> 'Two printed means for LSD 100 µg in Table 1 lie outside their own ranges, and the pharmacokinetics paragraph misprints a range (Table S7)'; amend the extracted text of the anchor on Table 1 (p. 1183) to match.

items.finding: Guesses after each session / at the end of the study (percent of 28): placebo named correctly 100% / 96% (4% took it for LSD 100 µg at the end). Psilocybin 15 mg: correct 64% / 75%; as psilocybin 30 mg 7% / 21%; as LSD 100 µg 29% / 0%; as LSD 200 µg 0% / 4%. Psilocybin 30 mg: correct 57% / 57%; as placebo 0% / 4%; as 15 mg 29% / 7%; as LSD 100 µg 0% / 18%; as LSD 200 µg 14% / 14%. LSD 100 µg: correct 57% / 61%; as psilocybin 15 mg 11% / 18%; as 30 mg 11% / 7%; as LSD 200 µg 21% / 14%. LSD 200 µg: correct 61% / 68%; as psilocybin 15 mg 4% / 0%; as 30 mg 18% / 14%; as LSD 100 µg 18% / 18%. Editors' calculation, right drug (either dose): after the session 71%, 86%, 78% and 79%; at the end of the study 96%, 64%, 75% and 86% (psilocybin 15 mg, 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, 200 µg).
items.locator: Supplementary Table S8 (columns 'after Session' and 'after Study')
items.proposed_change: Card key finding 12 (index 11): replace '(time point not named...)' by 'placebo was named correctly in 100% of sessions after the session and by 96% at the end of the study (Table S8)'; reporting issue 4 (index 3): give the exact shares 71%, 86%, 78%, 79% after the session (96%, 64%, 75%, 86% at the end) instead of 'at least'. Claim statement and magnitude: 'at least 64%, 86%, 78% and 79%' -> '71%, 86%, 78% and 79% after the session' (the 64% for psilocybin 15 mg was a floor: 7% more took it for the higher psilocybin dose), and 'the dummy was recognised in 96% of sessions' -> 'in every session (100%) when asked after it, and by 96% at the end of the study'.

items.finding: The round-2 note recorded for the card's next revision ('cross-drug confusion was commoner at the end of the study') does not hold for all conditions: guesses of the other drug went from 29% to 4% (psilocybin 15 mg), 14% to 32% (psilocybin 30 mg), 22% to 25% (LSD 100 µg) and 22% to 14% (LSD 200 µg) between after-session and end-of-study (editors' calculation from Table S8).
items.locator: Supplementary Table S8
items.proposed_change: Before that 'missed' note enters the card, reword it: 'at the end of the study, cross-drug confusion rose for psilocybin 30 mg and LSD 100 µg and fell for psilocybin 15 mg and LSD 200 µg (Table S8)'.

items.finding: Complaint checklist, number of the 28 reporting each complaint in 0-12 h (placebo, psilocybin 15 mg, psilocybin 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, LSD 200 µg): headache 8, 14, 18, 13, 13 (12-24 h: 6, 10, 14, 8, 10); fatigue 16, 23, 25, 16, 19; lack of concentration 0, 17, 15, 18, 22; loss of appetite 0, 7, 18, 11, 15; balance disorders 0, 9, 16, 10, 16; nausea 0, 7, 9, 8, 9; trembling 0, 2, 5, 13, 14; tendency to cry 0, 4, 11, 8, 7; anxiety 0, 2, 6, 4, 7 (12-24 h: 0, 1, 1, 0, 4); bruxism 0, 2, 1, 7, 10. No tests of these counts. They are far higher than the adverse events reported spontaneously within 48 h that the claim quotes (headache in 4 people after psilocybin and 3 after LSD).

items.proposed_change: Claim 'Unwanted effects' sentence: add the checklist counts (by condition, with the dummy's count beside them, and 'no tests of these counts'), e.g. 'on a checklist, headache within 12 hours was reported by 18 of 28 after psilocybin 30 mg and 13 after either LSD dose, against 8 on the dummy'; say that the 48-hour figures are spontaneous reports. Card: add the Table S6 counts to key finding 8 (index 7) or a new key finding.

items.finding: The complaint totals are in Table S5, not Table S6 (which holds item counts): acute 0-12 h 1.9 ± 0.6 (placebo), 8.9 ± 1.4, 13 ± 1.6, 12 ± 2.0, 15 ± 2.0; subacute 12-24 h 1.3 ± 0.3, 2.4 ± 0.5, 4.1 ± 0.8, 3.1 ± 0.6, 4.8 ± 0.8 (psilocybin 15 mg, 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, 200 µg); acute: all four above placebo (p < 0.001), psilocybin 15 mg below LSD 200 µg (p < 0.01), psilocybin 30 mg and LSD 200 µg not different; subacute: only psilocybin 30 mg (p < 0.01) and LSD 200 µg (p < 0.001) above placebo.

items.finding: Mood scale statistics behind the claim's 'emotional excitation' sentence: AMRS emotional excitation ΔEmax -0.9 ± 0.4 (placebo), 2.5 ± 0.6, 3.2 ± 0.8, 6.5 ± 1.1, 6.1 ± 0.9 (psilocybin 15 mg, 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, 200 µg); psilocybin 30 mg below LSD 100 µg (p < 0.01) and LSD 200 µg (p < 0.05); psilocybin 15 mg below both (p < 0.001). One further difference between psilocybin 30 mg and LSD 100 µg: AMRS dreaminess ΔEmin (-0.1 ± 0.2 against 1.1 ± 0.4, p < 0.05). Psilocybin 30 mg against either LSD dose: no difference on any of the 18 5D-ASC rows (Table S1) or 30 visual analogue rows (Table S3); against LSD 200 µg, MEQ ineffability only (MEQ30 p < 0.05, MEQ43 p < 0.01; Table S2).

items.finding: Tables S1 and S3 confirm the card's other subjective-effect statements: LSD 200 against 100 µg on visual analogue ego dissolution 67 ± 6.3 against 87 ± 4.7 % (p < 0.05); psilocybin 15 mg below LSD 200 µg on any drug effect (68 ± 4.8 against 95 ± 2.1), good drug effect, feeling stimulated, perception of time (ΔEmin) and ego dissolution (each p < 0.001) and talkative (ΔEmin, p < 0.01); 5D-ASC total 19 ± 2.6 against 35 ± 2.9 (p < 0.001); psilocybin 30 mg above 15 mg on any drug effect (p < 0.001), good drug effect (p < 0.01), stimulated (p < 0.01) and ego dissolution (p < 0.001).
items.locator: Supplementary Table S3 (VAS) and Table S1 (5D-ASC)
items.proposed_change: None needed; the editor may add the tables to the locators of key finding 3 (index 2) and of the claim's anchor on pp. 1182-1183.

items.finding: Pupil light reflex and hormones. Constriction to light (Emin) 1.5 ± 0.1 mm (placebo), 1.3, 1.0, 1.4 and 1.3 (each ± 0.1; psilocybin 15 mg, 30 mg, LSD 100 µg, 200 µg): psilocybin 30 mg impaired it more than psilocybin 15 mg (p < 0.01), LSD 100 µg (p < 0.001) and LSD 200 µg (p < 0.05); against placebo only psilocybin 30 mg (p < 0.001) and LSD 200 µg (p < 0.05). Hormones: cortisol rose with all four active conditions (p < 0.001); prolactin and oxytocin did not rise significantly with psilocybin 15 mg (changes 8.7 ± 42 mU/L and 8.3 ± 4.9 pg/mL against -128 ± 38 and -14 ± 8 on placebo), and prolactin rose with LSD 200 µg only at p < 0.05.
items.locator: Supplementary Table S5, rows 'Pupil contraction (mm)', 'Cortisol', 'Prolactin', 'Oxytocin'; Fig. S4 legend
items.proposed_change: Card: settle the round-2 'missed' note on the pupil (psilocybin impaired the light reflex more than LSD) with these values in key finding 8 (index 7); key finding 10 (index 9) -> 'cortisol rose with every active dose; prolactin and oxytocin with psilocybin 30 mg and both LSD doses, not significantly with psilocybin 15 mg'. Not needed for the claim.

items.finding: Every table gives N = 28 and F(4,108) (Table 1 in the article F(3,81)): complete data for all 28 on every outcome. The tables hold 94 outcome rows (Table S1 18, S2 14, S3 30, S4 16, S5 16), plus 5 in the article's Table 1: 99 outcomes, each with an omnibus F and up to 10 Tukey comparisons, without correction across outcomes (editors' count). The Supplementary Methods name four 'primary VAS outcome measures' (any drug effect, good drug effect, bad drug effect, ego dissolution) besides the 5D-ASC as the primary outcome measure. A 'complete mystical experience' (60% or more on every MEQ30 factor) is defined but its rate is not reported.
items.locator: Supplementary Tables S1-S5 (headers and footnotes); Supplementary Methods, paragraphs 'Visual Analog Scales', '5 Dimensions of Altered States of Consciousness' and 'Mystical Effects Questionnaire'
items.proposed_change: Card: outcomes.n_outcomes_tested 42 -> 99 and multiplicity_correction updated with this count; sample.attrition -> 'N = 28 with F(4,108) in every supplementary table: complete data'; preregistration_detail: add the four primary visual analogue outcomes (registry still not read); selective_reporting: the unreported rate of complete mystical experiences.

items.finding: Table S2 labels every MEQ row '% score', but the subscale rows cannot be percentages of their maximum: the MEQ30 total for LSD 200 µg is 47% while its four subscales are printed as 27, 15, 17 and 12, and a total percentage cannot exceed all of its parts. Fig. S1 (same data, '% scale maximum') shows those subscales at roughly 36% to 78% (editors' approximate reading), with the total at about 47%. The subscale rows of MEQ30 and MEQ43 look like raw scores. Also minor: in Table S7 the psilocin 30 mg AUC∞ geometric mean, 131, lies outside its own 95% CI (107-130).
items.locator: Supplementary Table S2 (all subscale rows) against Fig. S1; Table S7, row 'Psilocin 30 mg', column 'AUC∞'
items.proposed_change: Card: add as a reporting issue; never quote Table S2 subscale values as percentages (use Fig. S1, approximately, or call them scores).

items.finding: Effect-time curve of 'any drug effect' (mean ± SEM, range; MDMA, LSD, LSD with MDMA; F(2,46)): duration 4.3 ± 0.4 (0.7-10), 8.4 ± 0.4 (5.1-11), 9.9 ± 0.8 h (5.1-21), the combination longer than LSD (p < 0.05); offset 4.9 ± 0.4 (1.0-11), 8.9 ± 0.4 (5.7-12), 10 ± 0.8 h (5.7-21); onset 0.5, 0.4, 0.4 h (F = 2.2, p = 0.117); time to maximum 1.9, 2.2, 2.3 h (combination range 0.5-7.0); maximal effect 64 ± 5.6, 90 ± 3.1, 93 ± 2.6%; area under the effect curve 182 ± 28, 494 ± 33, 575 ± 46 (combination not marked as different from LSD). With both drugs at least one person's effects lasted up to 21 h, against at most 11 h with LSD alone.
items.locator: Supplement p. 15, Table S5
items.proposed_change: Card key finding 4 (index 3): add Table S5 values ± SEM and ranges to the locator and finding. Claim: the flag_note left the 1.5-hour longer duration to the editor; Table S5 adds that the longest effect lasted 21 h with both drugs against 11 h with LSD alone, which may belong in the claim as a risk fact (editor's decision; no timing or dosing advice).

items.finding: Guesses during (2.5 h), after (24 h) the session and after the study: placebo named correctly 96%, 96%, 100%; MDMA 83%, 96%, 100%; LSD 71%, 58%, 75%; LSD with MDMA 37.5%, 46%, 75%; the combination was taken for LSD alone in 50%, 46%, 25%, and LSD for the combination in 25%, 38%, 25%. Placebo and MDMA alone were thus almost always recognised; only LSD and the combination were confused.
items.locator: Supplement p. 17, Table S8
items.proposed_change: Card risk_of_bias, domain 'Deviations from intended interventions': replace 'placebo recognition is not reported in the main text' by 'placebo was recognised in 96-100% and MDMA alone in 83-100% of sessions (Table S8); only LSD and the combination were often confused, so blinding was partial for the comparison the claim rests on and near absent against placebo or MDMA'. outcomes.assessor_blinding: add the placebo and MDMA figures.

items.finding: Primary outcomes: the Supplementary Methods name the primary visual analogue outcomes ('good drug effect', 'trust', 'open', 'bad drug effects', 'fear'), call the AMRS 'a primary measure', and the 5D-ASC 'the primary outcome measure'. These match the stated primary hypothesis (more good drug effects, well-being, openness and trust, fewer bad drug effects and less anxiety with the combination than with LSD alone). On every one of them the combination did not differ from LSD alone: trust ΔEmax 31 ± 3.8 against 38 ± 3.1 (NS) and open 26 ± 3.7 against 32 ± 3.7 (NS) (Table S1); AMRS well-being 4.9 ± 1.0 against 4.4 ± 0.9 and anxiety 1.0 ± 0.3 against 1.1 ± 0.3 (NS) (Table S4); good drug effect, bad drug effect and fear NS (article Table 1); all 18 5D-ASC rows NS (Table S2).
items.locator: Supplement p. 1, Supplementary Methods, paragraphs 'Visual Analog Scales', 'Adjective Mood Rating Scale' and '5 Dimension of Altered States of Consciousness'; p. 11, Table S1; p. 12, Table S2; p. 14, Table S4

items.finding: Mood scale peaks (ΔEmax; placebo, MDMA, LSD, LSD with MDMA): emotional excitation -1.7 ± 0.6, 0.3 ± 0.7, 5.3 ± 1.0, 4.5 ± 1.1; introversion 0.1 ± 0.3, 1.9 ± 0.3, 4.8 ± 0.6, 5.1 ± 0.5; anxiety -0.3 ± 0.2, 0 ± 0.3, 1.0 ± 0.3, 1.1 ± 0.3; depression -0.3 ± 0.1, 0.6 ± 0.3, 1.6 ± 0.4, 1.5 ± 0.3: LSD and the combination above MDMA alone on all four (p < 0.05 to p < 0.001) and not different from each other on any AMRS scale. MEQ 'distressing experience' 21 ± 4.4 (LSD) against 18 ± 5.1 % (combination) and 'nadir' 22 ± 3.3 against 19 ± 4.3, NS. The late lower mood with the combination that the discussion describes as a trend is visible only in Fig. S3, where the combination's mean depression and anxiety ratings stay above LSD's from about 9 to 24 h and its well-being dips below LSD's at 6-9 h (values not extracted); no test at these time points is given and the peaks did not differ.

items.proposed_change: Card: settle the round-2 'missed' note (more emotional excitation, introversion, anxiety and depression than MDMA alone) with these values; key finding 11 (index 10) note -> 'Fig. S3 shows the direction; no test at time points; peak ratings did not differ (Table S4)'. Claim: after 'trend-level, non-significant signs of lower well-being and more depressed mood', add 'shown only in a figure, without tests at those hours; the highest ratings did not differ'; the distressing-experience score (21 against 18, not significant) supports 'did not significantly lower the unwanted effects'.

items.finding: Metabolites (geometric mean, 95% CI; no tests): O-H-LSD, the main LSD metabolite, AUC∞ 2.4 (2.0-2.7) with LSD alone against 3.3 (3.0-3.7) ng·h/mL with MDMA, half-life 8.7 (7.6-9.9) against 10 (8.9-12) h, CL/F 43 against 30 L/h. Editors' calculation with the article's parent-drug AUC∞ (14 and 19): the metabolite-to-LSD exposure ratio is about 0.17 in both conditions. MDA (AUC∞ 287 against 275 ng·h/mL) and HMMA (2482 against 2375) were similar with and without LSD; some MDMA-alone values come from 23 or 22 people.

items.finding: Outcome count and completeness: the supplementary tables add 65 outcome rows (Table S1 16, S2 18, S3 17, S4 8, S5 6) to the 26 of the article's Table 1, 91 in all, each with an omnibus F and pairwise Tukey tests, without correction across outcomes (editors' count); N = 24 in every table (F(3,69), F(2,46)); pupil data from 23 (Fig. S4 legend). Fig. S4 confirms that the light reflex was reduced more with the combination and with MDMA alone than with LSD, settling the round-2 'missed' note on the pupil. The 5D-ASC anxiety subscale: 9.9 ± 3.4 (LSD) and 9.3 ± 4.4 % (combination), F(3,69) = 3.8, p = 0.014, with no pairwise difference, consistent with the round-2 note (trend p = 0.073 in the text). The visual analogue item 'my focus is directed inward/outward', listed in the Supplementary Methods, is reported in neither Table 1 nor Table S1; Table S1 labels the first 'Happy' row ΔEmin where ΔEmax is meant.

items.finding: Appendix 3, the quality form, is read: 16 points in four parts. Global: a focused question (1). Selection: recruitment from several places (1), eligibility described (1), participants described at intake (1), number injecting before treatment given (1). Outcome: instrument for use or dependence named (1), follow-up over 70% (1), crude and standardised mortality rates (1), person-years (1) and expected deaths (1) reported, periods in and out of treatment clearly defined (1). Analysis and confounding: age and sex (1), HIV (1) and HCV (1) identified and taken into account; overdose results specified (1); results by time period (1). It assesses confounding (three baseline factors) and some selection bias (completeness of follow-up), and partly exposure (defined periods); it does not assess how deaths and causes were ascertained, selective reporting, or selection by non-random exits from treatment, and it sums reporting items (rates, expected deaths, time-period results) with bias items into one score.
